Presidential Gubernatorial Aradel’s ₦2.46tn cash generation moves it to net cash position The performance reflects the increased scale of its operations following the consolidation of ND Western and Renaissance, alongside stronger production and substantial cash generation. by Press Release November 16, 2026 Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Add us on Google Aradel Holdings Plc generated ₦2.46 trillion in net cash from operating activities in the nine months ended 30 September 2026, marking a significant improvement in its financial position as the Group moved from a net debt position of ₦475.1 billion at the end of 2025 to a net cash position of ₦532.3 billion. The performance reflects the increased scale of its operations following the consolidation of ND Western and Renaissance, alongside stronger production and substantial cash generation.
The results show a significantly enlarged business, with revenue rising to ₦3.95 trillion, EBITDA reaching ₦2.10 trillion and average production increasing to 144.7barrels of oil equivalent per day (kboepd). The EBITDA margin also improved to 53 per cent from 49 per cent a year earlier, while unit field operating costs declined by 28 per cent to US$7.9 per barrel of oil equivalent from US$11.0, reflecting improved operational efficiency across the enlarged asset base.
A major factor behind the results is the consolidation of ND Western and Renaissance following the completion of the acquisitions on December 31, 2025. This is the first reporting period in which both businesses are fully reflected in the Group’s results, significantly expanding its production capacity, revenue base and operational footprint.
Average production reached 144.7 kboepd, compared with 24.0 kboepd in the corresponding period of 2025. Crude oil production averaged 57.9 kbopd, while gas production rose to 503.6 million standard cubic feet per day, supported by expanded processing capacity, sustained pipeline availability and continued customer demand. Revenue grew by 633 per cent, with crude oil and ga the major contributors
The Group also recorded ₦253.1 billion in other income, principally from crude handling fees generated through third-party use of its evacuation infrastructure. These contributions highlight the broader revenue opportunities within Aradel’s enlarged operations, including the utilisation of its infrastructure by other industry players.
Refining performance remained an area of operational focus, with net refined product output declining 18 per cent to 194.2 million litres and refinery utilisation standing at 45 per cent. However, output improved sequentially in each quarter following the first, reflecting progress in restoring and improving refinery operations.
One of the most significant outcomes of the nine-month performance was the Group’s ability to convert its expanded operations into substantial operating cash. Aradel generated ₦2.46 trillion in net cash from operating activities, compared with ₦205.4 billion in the corresponding period of 2025.

This provided substantial funding for the Group’s investment and financing obligations, including ₦570.6 billion in capital expenditure, ₦580.5 billion in interest and principal repayments, ₦81.4 billion in lease payments, ₦110.5 billion in dividends and ₦543.9 billion in earnout payments.
The resulting improvement in the balance sheet saw Aradel transition from net debt of ₦475.1 billion at the end of 2025 to a net cash position of ₦532.3 billion at September 30, 2026. Total borrowings declined by approximately 25 per cent following the full repayment of two facilities in the first quarter.
The Group ended September with cash and cash equivalents of approximately ₦2.00 trillion and an additional ₦41.5 billion in restricted cash. Including restricted cash, total cash for the net cash calculation stood at approximately ₦2.04 trillion, against total borrowings of ₦1.51 trillion.
The strength of this performance is further demonstrated by operating cash flow before working-capital movements, which stood at approximately ₦2.48 trillion. This indicates that the Group’s substantial cash generation was supported primarily by its operating performance, rather than being dependent on favourable working-capital movements.
While operational performance and cash generation strengthened, reported earnings were affected by acquisition-related costs and the tax profile of the enlarged Group. Profit after tax stood at ₦43.3 billion, compared with ₦245.1 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Profit attributable to shareholders was ₦141.5 billion, compared with ₦242.9 billion, while earnings per share declined to ₦32.57 from ₦55.90. The difference between Group profit and profit attributable to shareholders reflects a ₦98.2 billion loss attributable to non-controlling interests.
A significant contributor to the reported earnings outcome was the earnout arrangement arising from Renaissance’s acquisition of Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC). Under the arrangement, the seller retains an economic interest in a defined perimeter of Renaissance’s assets, with payments calculated by reference to net revenues generated within that perimeter. The related contingent consideration is recognised within finance costs, resulting in a ₦529.1 billion charge during the nine months. The Group also made cash payments of ₦543.9 billion under the arrangement, with the outstanding liability standing at ₦1.32 trillion as of September 30, 2026.
The enlarged Group’s tax expense also increased to ₦721.4 billion from ₦55.6 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, reflecting the higher tax rates associated with ND Western and Renaissance. Together, the earnout charge and increased tax expense contributed to the difference between the Group’s operating performance and reported profit.
On an alternative performance measure, Aradel reported profit after tax before the earnout charge of ₦572.4 billion, representing a 134 per cent increase over the prior year. The company attributes no tax effect to the earnout adjustment and presents this figure to provide additional insight into performance before the charge. It is important to distinguish this measure from reported IFRS profit.
The Board considers that the earnout arrangement no longer reflects the balanced participation originally intended by the parties. Aradel, alongside other Renaissance shareholders, are said to be engaging the seller on the matter. Without prejudice to these discussions, the earnout is expected to continue to accrue for the remainder of 2026.
Building on the operational improvements recorded during the period, Aradel has raised its full-year 2026 production guidance to between 140,000 and 150,000 boepd, from the previous range of 110,000 to 140,000 boepd, following production levels above its earlier expectations.
Management expects EBITDA, operating cash generation and liquidity to remain robust after earnout payments. Its priorities include optimising the enlarged asset base, improving uptime, growing production and maintaining disciplined capital allocation.
Aradel’s nine-month results reflect the growing scale and financial capacity of its expanded operations. The Group has significantly increased production, strengthened its operating cash generation, improved operational efficiency and transitioned into a net cash position. With higher production guidance and an expanded portfolio of oil, gas and refining assets, the Group enters the final quarter of 2026 with a stronger financial foundation and increased capacity to pursue its growth priorities. Its ability to sustain this momentum while managing acquisition-related obligations will remain important as it continues to consolidate the benefits of its enlarged asset base.
